scope: Level 02 P0 art for V4: four stele bases, the shared rotating ring, three cranks, the gate leaf in both states with its latch, and four dark receiving mouths.
style: Painterly pixel-cluster fantasy RPG, front-facing orthographic top-down view with a slight visible top face, cold blue-grey slate, dark teal moss, old honey brass, soft upper-left light. Follows the Level 01 V4 direction (assets/levels/01-forgotten-forest-edge/v4/ART-DIRECTION.md).

revisions.reason: The first sheet filled the stele face with the glyph, so the rotating ring covered it. Regenerated with the glyph at about 40 percent of the face width and a wide blank stone border for the ring to sit around.

In the first sheet the cranks were post-and-wheel scenes; at 16x16 the shaped hub disappeared. Regenerated as face-on wheels with a large bright hub, and the hub mark is stamped at 1x by prepare-assets.py because a downscaled painting cannot stay legible at that size.

prompts.sheet: 1536x1024, 1 row x 4 cells (only the ring cell is used)
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY FOUR isolated mechanism sprites in ONE horizontal row, evenly spaced, very generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, floor, shadow or UI. Flat sheet, not a mockup.
Cell 1: the ROTATING RING that sits over a stele face, reading at 28x28 logical pixels but drawn large. A thin worn honey-brass ring with a hollow FULLY TRANSPARENT centre, one raised rectangular NOTCH tab on the top edge, two small rivets, dark patina in the recess. The ring must read as a rim that turns in 120-degree steps; it is not a solid disc and carries no glyph.
Cells 2 to 4: three CRANK wheels that stand on the forest floor, each reading at 16x16 logical pixels but drawn large, each with the SAME body: a short dark wooden post, a small brass axle, a flat round wheel face with a worn rim and a low handle knob at the side. Same size, baseline and lighting in all three; ONLY the shaped hub at the centre differs so the three are told apart by silhouette, never by colour:
cell 2 hub is TWO CROSSED BARS forming an X;
cell 3 hub is a THREE-PRONGED FORK forming a Y;
cell 4 hub is a SHORT ZIGZAG BAR forming a Z.
Front-facing orthographic with slight visible tops, crisp painterly pixel clusters, cold dark wood, aged honey brass, faint moss at the foot. No lettering of any kind; the hubs are physical metal shapes.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY THREE isolated crank wheels in ONE horizontal row, evenly spaced, generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, floor or UI. Flat sheet, not a mockup.
Each crank reads at 16x16 logical pixels but is drawn LARGE and fills its cell. It is a FACE-ON view of a small mechanism wheel standing on the forest floor: a short dark wooden post stub visible only at the bottom edge, a thick worn honey-brass rim around a dark aged-wood wheel face, and a bright raised brass HUB at the dead centre.
The hub is the identifier and must be big, simple and bright: it covers about two thirds of the wheel face, is clearly raised above the wood, and is polished brass with a strong dark outline so it stays readable when the whole sprite is only 16 pixels wide. Value contrast matters more than detail: bright brass against near-black wood.
Cell 1 hub: TWO CROSSED BARS forming an X.
Cell 2 hub: a THREE-PRONGED FORK forming a Y.
Cell 3 hub: a Z-SHAPED BAR with two square bends.
All three share the exact same wheel diameter, rim, post stub, baseline, facing and lighting; only the hub shape changes. Front-facing orthographic, crisp painterly pixel clusters, soft upper-left light, faint moss only on the post stub. No lettering anywhere: each hub is one solid physical metal casting, thick and blocky, not a thin drawn symbol.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production game sprite sheet on a truly transparent background: EXACTLY THREE isolated sprites in ONE horizontal row, evenly spaced, generous transparent gutters, nothing touching a cell edge. No text, numbers, labels, arrows, floor, cast shadow or UI. Flat sheet, not a mockup.
The gate is a NARROW VERTICAL SLIDING LEAF, 8 wide and 40 tall logical pixels, drawn large inside its cell at that tall narrow proportion: dark aged wood planks bound by two thin honey-brass straps, a small square brass keeper plate halfway up, chipped corners. It is NOT an arch, NOT double doors, NOT a portcullis.
Cell 1 GATE CLOSED: the leaf fills the full 8x40 opening, planks tight, straps level, bottom edge seated on a barely visible brass sill.
Cell 2 GATE OPEN: the SAME leaf pulled straight up into its pocket, so the visible part is a compressed gathered bundle at the very top of the cell and the lower four fifths of the cell are COMPLETELY TRANSPARENT empty passage; keep the leaf's outer width identical to cell 1.
Cell 3 LATCH, reading at 8x8 logical pixels but drawn large: a small brass hook lever on a square slate foot, hooked end pointing left over a short steel keeper, a seated pin through the hook. It must read as a mechanical catch that holds a raised gate, not a door handle.
Crisp painterly pixel clusters, cold dark wood, aged honey brass, faint green moss only on the outer edges, soft upper-left light. Same material family and scale across the three.
